name: Refine should not work in the main working tree

current_round.prompt:
From: Ethan Jacobson <ethan.jacobson@insurity.com>
Subject: Refine should not work in the main working tree

Body:
To allow concurrent manual development by the developer, refine should always use a dedicated worktree.  I thought it did that, but apparently not.  Here is an answer from Claude when I asked about some main working tree changes that appeared:


What the changes are: the configuration-screen filter/sort feature — a "Filter by {key}" search box (config-filter-input, filterText(), onFilterChange), reworked sorting in data-grid.component.ts, and a new config-filter-and-sort.spec.ts replacing the old screen spec. That's your refine goal's work.

Where they live: only in your main working tree (/insurity/ProSuite). I checked every worktree — no refine worktree has them — and git log --all -S 'config-filter-input' finds them on no branch at all (not insurity-claims, not origin, not any refine/<id>/round-N).

Your assumption is off — this goal is running in your MAIN worktree, not a separate one. The tell: minutes ago, right after I stash-popped them, those files were unstaged ( M); now they're back to MM (staged again). Something re-staged them since — i.e., the refine goal is actively editing and staging in main right now. (You do have 7 goals isolated under .git/refine-worktrees/, so refine can use worktrees — but this particular config-screen goal is operating directly on main.)

Why they haven't been pushed: because they've never been committed. The goal is mid-round — refine only creates a commit (Implement <goal> round N) when a round completes, and only then does it land on a branch and get pushed. Until then it's live working-tree state, so there's literally nothing on origin to push.

One thing worth flagging: because this goal shares the main worktree with everything else, my push operation earlier had to stash/restore these exact files (the merge wouldn't proceed with them dirty). I restored them and the goal has since continued — so no harm done — but it means your git operations and this running goal are working in the same tree simultaneously, which is inherently race-prone. If you can, it's safer to let that goal finish its round (and commit) before doing manual git work in main, or run it in an isolated worktree like your other goals. Nothing to fix right now; the work is intact and will push itself when the round lands.


[cid:insurity-small2_2f81c33c-d951-4e5c-a467-1113541ca22c.jpg]
Ethan Jacobson
Ethan.Jacobson@insurity.com

goal.name: Refine should not work in the main working tree

governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.
Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching; keep non-external CLI/API work under 50ms.
Update affected documentation—especially `src/intent/*`—without changing its established format.
Use installed coding-agent CLIs for coding-agent capabilities; do not reimplement them.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Foundation, Capabilities, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.
guidance_candidates.name: Intent and architecture
guidance_candidates.rule: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.
guidance_candidates.name: Cohesive code files
guidance_candidates.rule: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

agent_context.workflow_summary: Refine gives this Goal Agent an isolated worktree and a finalized implementation plan. Implement the current Round and report evidence; a separate agent will review and correct the candidate in Quality, then an independent Governance gate will verify policy and integrate the exact passing commit before human Review. Do not directly advance Goal state, approve, merge, or push.

checklist.description: Extend the existing Git worktree capability to require a registered, canonically resolved linked checkout in the expected repository and owned location with the phase's recorded branch or commit, rejecting the main checkout and unrelated worktrees even when their branch matches.

Enforce this workspace requirement during initial creation, restart, retained recovery handoffs, and exact-candidate checkout reuse, recreating missing managed checkouts from durable branch and candidate evidence while reporting ambiguous ownership or branch conflicts without moving, stashing, staging, or deleting existing work.

Resolve agent_subpath to an existing directory canonically contained within the admitted worktree and carry that workspace explicitly through planning, implementation, correction, Governance, and recovery launches, including provider-session resumes and fresh-launch fallbacks.

Recheck workspace ownership and Git identity at agent launch and before Refine stages, commits, or refreshes candidate changes so stale paths, changed registrations, and branch switches fail through the existing recoverable infrastructure-error boundary.

Remove inherited Git repository and index redirection variables from managed Goal and Quality processes and their Git invocations while preserving deliberate per-command overrides needed by existing isolated Git operations.

Route legacy Quality execution that currently selects the main checkout through the existing exact-source-candidate reconciliation worktree path while preserving retained proof, candidate identity, and terminal failed-result semantics.

Update the affected Goal Agent and worktree intent pages to make automated workspace isolation mandatory and describe ownership-conflict recovery while preserving the documented integration and human Review handoff.

result.summary: Keep all automated Goal authoring, checks, corrections, and recovery in dedicated Refine-owned worktrees so concurrent manual development is protected from unfinished Goal edits and staging in the developer's checkout.
